title: NeuVSA: A Unified and Efficient Accelerator for Neural Vector Search
problem: Neural Vector Search (NVS) systems require both a neural embedding stage and a vector search stage, but existing accelerators treat these as separate compute kernels with incompatible memory access patterns, causing insufficient parallelization, frequent data access conflicts, and poor scheduling.
motivation: Information retrieval increasingly relies on NVS for superior recall quality, yet the embedding-search separation creates a fundamental efficiency gap that cannot be resolved by simply combining existing accelerators.
method: NeuVSA uses Product Quantization (PQ) to unify both the embedding and search stages—PQ compresses vectors by splitting them into parts and looking each part up in a shared codebook. Both the codebook and the search index are trained together in one unified process, learning the optimal setup for both simultaneously. The custom ASIC contains multiple coordinated sub-accelerators that use structured index assignment and an elastic on-chip buffer to prevent data conflicts and maximize throughput, achieving 4.6% better recall and 43.5% better accuracy than LUT-NN.
key_novelty: NeuVSA unifies embedding and vector search into a single system by designing the algorithm and hardware together around Product Quantization, eliminating the traditional separation between these two stages.
contributions: Learned PQ-based unified NVS algorithm with end-to-end joint codebook+index training
Homogeneous ASIC accelerator exploiting all parallelism of the unified algorithm
Elastic on-chip buffer and structured index assignment to eliminate data access conflicts
2.82x-416x lower latency and up to 49.6x higher throughput vs. CPU/GPU/DFX+ANNA/PQA+ANNA; 65.2% area reduction vs. PQA+ANNA

metrics.speedup: 2.82x-416.17x lower latency over CPU, GPU, DFX+ANNA, PQA+ANNA
metrics.other: 49.60x higher throughput over CPU; 10.57x over GPU; 65.2% area reduction vs. PQA+ANNA; 4.6% recall improvement over separated strategy

limitations: Evaluation is limited to product-quantization-based NVS; graph-based ANN search (HNSW, etc.) is not addressed.
primary_theme: Unified neural vector search accelerator via PQ-based algorithm-architecture co-design
